# Settings reference

Every setting is an environment variable (or a line in `.env`). Nothing else reads the
environment. Secrets are redacted in every output, including the config digest stored
with each run. Any host that receives a conversation or a key must also be listed in
`OPSEVAL_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

| Variable | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPSEVAL_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | text | empty | Comma-separated hostnames that may receive credentials or conversations. |
| `OPSEVAL_DOTENV` | bool | `True` | Read ``.env`` from the working directory. Set ``OPSEVAL_DOTENV=false`` in the real environment (a ``.env`` cannot switch itself off) to ignore it, as the GitHub action does unless asked, so a checked-out repository cannot configure the run (ADR-0058). |
| `OPSEVAL_STATIC_TOKEN` | secret | unset (secret) | A bearer token sent to the agent as is, when the profile does not mint its own. |
| `OPSEVAL_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | The HS256 key for profiles that mint short-lived tokens per attempt (ADR-0012). |
| `OPSEVAL_CREDENTIALS` | text | empty | A credential provider plugin to supply the agent's tokens, by entry-point name (``opseval.credentials``, ADR-0046). Installing one changes nothing until it is named here. It replaces ``OPSEVAL_STATIC_TOKEN``; a tenant's own ``token_env`` still wins. |
| `OPSEVAL_SIMULATOR_BASE_URL` | text | unset | OpenAI-compatible endpoint of the LLM that plays the customer (host allowlisted). |
| `OPSEVAL_SIMULATOR_API_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | API key for the simulator endpoint, if it needs one. |
| `OPSEVAL_SIMULATOR_MODEL` | text | unset | Model the simulator uses. Without it, only scripted scenarios run. |
| `OPSEVAL_JUDGE_BASE_URL` | text | unset | OpenAI-compatible endpoint of the LLM judges. Its host must be allowlisted. |
| `OPSEVAL_JUDGE_API_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | API key for the judge endpoint, if it needs one. |
| `OPSEVAL_JUDGE_MODEL` | text | unset | Model the judges use. Without it, judge scores are not measured. |
| `OPSEVAL_SIMULATOR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | number | `300.0` | The most one simulator call (an opening, a reply, a checkpoint decision) may take. Simulator time is off the agent's clock; overrunning this is a harness error. |
| `OPSEVAL_JUDGE_CONCURRENCY` | integer | `4` | How many judge ballots may be in flight at once. |
| `OPSEVAL_JUDGE_INDEPENDENCE` | `error` \| `warn` \| `off` | `error` | What to do when a judge and the model it grades share a vendor family (ADR-0016). ``error`` refuses the run at launch (exit 3), ``warn`` scores but marks the results degraded, ``off`` skips the check. |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_PROVIDER` | text | `openai` | The text-to-speech provider: ``openai`` (the built-in OpenAI-compatible ``/v1/audio/speech`` client) or the name of an ``opseval.tts`` plugin. Only the named one is imported; a name nothing provides is refused (exit 3), never replaced by another. |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_URL` | text | unset | Base URL of the TTS provider (``{url}/v1/audio/speech`` for the built-in). Required for every provider, plugin included; its host must be allowlisted, and use TLS unless it is loopback. |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | API key for the TTS provider, if it needs one. |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_MODEL` | text | unset | TTS model, such as ``tts-1`` or ``gpt-4o-mini-tts``. |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_VOICE_MAP` | dict | `{}` | JSON object from a persona's voice name, or a language tag, to the provider's voice: ``{"calm_female": "nova", "ar": "onyx", "default": "alloy"}``. A voice is looked up by persona voice, then language, then ``default``; an unmapped persona voice is sent as is. |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_FORMAT` | `wav` \| `pcm` | `wav` | Audio format asked of the built-in TTS: ``wav`` (the rate is in the file) or ``pcm`` (raw PCM16 at ``OPSEVAL_TTS_PCM_RATE``). |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_PCM_RATE` | integer | `24000` | The sample rate of raw ``pcm`` TTS audio (OpenAI sends 24 kHz). |
| `OPSEVAL_TTS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | number | `30.0` | The most one TTS call may take, retries included. Off the agent's clock; overrunning it is a harness error (``TtsError``), never the agent's timeout. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_PROVIDER` | text | `openai` | The speech-to-text provider: ``openai`` (the built-in OpenAI-compatible ``/v1/audio/transcriptions`` client) or the name of an ``opseval.stt`` plugin. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_URL` | text | unset | Base URL of the STT provider (``{url}/v1/audio/transcriptions`` for the built-in). Required for every provider, plugin included. Allowlisted, TLS off loopback. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | API key for the STT provider, if it needs one. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_MODEL` | text | unset | STT model, such as ``whisper-1``. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | number | `60.0` | The most one STT call may take, retries included. Off the agent's clock; overrunning it is a harness error (``SttError``), never the agent's timeout (ADR-0053). |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_MIN_CONFIDENCE` | number | `0.5` | A transcript below this confidence marks the attempt's judge scores degraded (ADR-0053). A provider that reports no confidence is not measured, never 1.0. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_MAX_WER` | number | `0.25` | The STT health canary is healthy when its word error rate is at most this (ADR-0053). Calibrated per language pack later (ADR-0059). |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_WAV` | text | unset | A WAV of known speech for the STT canary when no TTS is configured to make one. Its words go in ``OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_TEXT`` and its language in ``OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_LANGUAGE``; one without the others is refused (exit 3). Without a TTS or this WAV, the canary is not run. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_TEXT` | text | unset | What ``OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_WAV`` says, word for word. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_LANGUAGE` | text | unset | The language ``OPSEVAL_STT_CANARY_WAV`` is spoken in, as a BCP-47 tag (``en``, ``ar-EG``). The STT is asked to hear the canary in this language, not the scenario's. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_SECOND_PROVIDER` | text | unset | An optional second STT check (ADR-0053): ``openai`` or an ``opseval.stt`` plugin. It must differ from the first in provider or model, or the run is refused (exit 3): the same STT twice proves nothing. Setting a second URL or model alone implies ``openai``. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_SECOND_URL` | text | unset | Base URL of the second STT. Allowlisted and preflighted like the first. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_SECOND_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | API key for the second STT, if it needs one. |
| `OPSEVAL_STT_SECOND_MODEL` | text | unset | Model of the second STT. |
| `OPSEVAL_RECORD_AUDIO` | `files` \| `hashes` | `files` | What a voice run keeps of each spoken turn (ADR-0053). ``files``: one WAV per speaker per turn under the run folder's ``audio/``, which needs ``OPSEVAL_AUDIO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`` (a voice can be biometric data), so without the key a voice run is refused (exit 3). ``hashes``: no bytes at all, only each turn's SHA-256, length, codec, rate and duration. |
| `OPSEVAL_AUDIO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | The key that seals recorded audio at rest with AES-256-GCM (ADR-0053), separate from the key that encrypts agent credentials: 32 random bytes as 64 hex characters or base64 (`opseval audio keygen`). Needs the ``opseval[voice]`` extra. The same key opens the files again (`opseval audio export`, the console's player); each file records the key's fingerprint, never the key. |
| `OPSEVAL_AUDIO_RETENTION_DAYS` | integer | `30` | ``opseval prune`` removes a finished run's recorded audio once the run is older than this many days, before the run itself goes (``OPSEVAL_RETENTION_DAYS``). The record keeps every turn's hash and transcript, and the audio reads as "pruned", never as missing. |
| `OPSEVAL_OTLP_SPANS_PATH` | text | unset | OTLP-JSON spans (a file or folder) for `traces.source: otlp-file` (ADR-0028). |
| `OPSEVAL_LANGFUSE_HOST` | text | unset | Langfuse base URL, for trace-backed tool checks and score pushing. Must be allowlisted. |
| `OPSEVAL_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` | text | unset | Langfuse public key. |
| `OPSEVAL_LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` | secret | unset (secret) | Langfuse secret key. |
| `OPSEVAL_TELEMETRY` | `auto` \| `true` \| `false` | `auto` | ``auto`` means on unless CI or DO_NOT_TRACK says otherwise, and only ever to an allowlisted endpoint. ``false`` disables it outright. |
| `OPSEVAL_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` | text | unset | Where telemetry counts go. None ships: nothing is sent until it is set and allowlisted. |
| `CI` or `OPSEVAL_CI` | bool | `False` | Telemetry is off in CI unless OPSEVAL_TELEMETRY=true is set explicitly. |
| `DO_NOT_TRACK` or `OPSEVAL_DO_NOT_TRACK` | bool | `False` | The community-standard opt-out. Honoured the same as OPSEVAL_TELEMETRY=false. |
| `OPSEVAL_WEBHOOK_URL` | secret | unset (secret) | Slack, Teams and Discord incoming-webhook URLs are credentials: redacted everywhere. |
| `OPSEVAL_GITHUB_ISSUES_REPO` | text | unset | ``owner/name``: open an issue for each failed critical or blocker scenario (ADR-0040). |
| `OPSEVAL_GITHUB_TOKEN` | secret | unset (secret) | Token for the issues sink; needs permission to write issues in that repository only. |
| `OPSEVAL_GITHUB_API_URL` | text | `https://api.github.com` | GitHub API base, for GitHub Enterprise. Its host must be allowlisted. |
| `OPSEVAL_GITHUB_ISSUES_MAX` | integer | `10` | Most issues opened or commented on per run, so a broken agent cannot flood a tracker. |
| `OPSEVAL_JIRA_URL` | text | unset | Jira base URL (``https://acme.atlassian.net`` or a Data Center host): open an issue for each failed critical or blocker scenario (ADR-0045). Its host must be allowlisted. |
| `OPSEVAL_JIRA_PROJECT` | text | unset | Project key the Jira sink writes to, such as ``AGENT``. |
| `OPSEVAL_JIRA_EMAIL` | text | unset | Account email for Jira Cloud (basic auth with an API token). Unset for Data Center, where the token is a personal access token sent as a bearer. |
| `OPSEVAL_JIRA_TOKEN` | secret | unset (secret) | Jira API token (Cloud) or personal access token (Data Center). |
| `OPSEVAL_JIRA_ISSUE_TYPE` | text | `Bug` | Issue type the Jira sink creates. |
| `OPSEVAL_JIRA_ISSUES_MAX` | integer | `10` | Most Jira issues opened or commented on per run. |
| `OPSEVAL_SINKS` | text | empty | Plugin sinks to enable, by name (comma-separated). Installing a package never starts publishing on its own: a plugin sink runs only when named here. |
| `OPSEVAL_LANGFUSE_PUSH_SCORES` | bool | `False` | Publish each finished run's verdicts to Langfuse as scores (ADR-0027). |
| `OPSEVAL_LANGFUSE_SCORE_NAME` | text | `opseval` | Name prefix for scores pushed to Langfuse. |
| `OPSEVAL_GATE_FAIL_ON_FLAKY` | bool | `False` | Make a flaky pass block the gate, whatever the suite's policy says. |
| `OPSEVAL_TENANTS_FILE` | text | unset | A test-tenant pool YAML: each scenario leases one tenant exclusively (ADR-0041). |
| `OPSEVAL_LANES` | integer | unset | Requested lanes. Actual = min(tenants, requested, lane_cap). |
| `OPSEVAL_LANE_CAP` | integer | `8` | The most lanes any run may use, however many tenants or lanes are asked for. |
| `OPSEVAL_TENANT_LOCK_DIR` | text | unset | Where tenant leases live. Default: a machine-wide directory keyed by the pool's tenant ids, because a path relative to the working directory would let two checkouts of the same pool lease the same account. |
| `OPSEVAL_TENANT_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` | number | `300.0` | A lease whose heartbeat is older than this may be reclaimed. Generous on purpose, and at least three heartbeats (30 s each), or every live lease would look dead. |
| `OPSEVAL_TENANT_WAIT_SECONDS` | number | `30.0` | How long to wait for a free tenant before skipping the scenario. |
| `OPSEVAL_REPORTS_DIR` | text | `reports` | Where run folders are written. |
| `OPSEVAL_RETENTION_DAYS` | integer | `90` | ``opseval prune`` deletes finished runs older than this many days (FR-SAF-06). |
| `OPSEVAL_SERVE_TOKEN` | secret | unset (secret) | The console API token. Random on every `opseval serve` start when unset (ADR-0031). |
| `OPSEVAL_CONSOLE_DIR` | text | unset | The built web console (``packages/console/dist``) for ``opseval serve`` to serve. When unset, a source checkout's build is found on its own (ADR-0034). |
| `OPSEVAL_DATABASE_URL` | secret | unset (secret) | Postgres for server mode: ``postgresql://user:password@host:5432/opseval``. It carries a password, so it is a secret. Its host must be allowlisted, and a host other than localhost needs TLS (``?ssl=require``, ``verify-ca`` or ``verify-full``). |
